conviction_note: Small positive lean from two sources. First, a hot August and September in the West and East South Central regions, against a quarter when YTD weather through June was -2c versus normal. Second, three utilities that reported in the past week (AEP, CNP, FE) beat, and AEP and CNP raised. Both are proxies; Q3 2025 shows weather beats buy little here (+0.46% on a narrowed guide); the 9.3% 20-day run-up has likely priced the peer tone; mild downside skew (+2.75). So p_up is 55 on abs_move 2.8, giving +0.28. The findings sum to +0.75 because they are sized one at a time and not fitted to the scaled number.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of about $1.72: chartmill $1.72 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/ETR/estimates) and MarketBeat $1.73 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/entergy-nyseetr-releases-fy-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-29/) agree. Benzinga shows $1.68 and KeyCorp $1.86 (single broker). Year-ago Q3 2025 adjusted EPS was $1.53 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65984/000006598425000126/earningsrelease3q25_ex991.htm). Company FY2026 guide is $4.25-4.45, affirmed 2026-07-29; YTD adjusted EPS is $1.90; FY consensus is about $4.40, the upper half of the guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65984/000006598426000279/earningsrelease2q26_ex991.htm).
positioning_check: About 17.85M shares short, 5.5 days to cover as of the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/etr); Equibles on 2026-08-20 had 20.3M, 4.4% of float, 6.7 days, falling (https://equibles.com/stocks/etr/shortinterest). Not crowded. Sealed baseline: 25d skew +2.75 vol pts (mild downside paid), put/call OI 0.35 (call-heavy), event-implied move 4.37%. The ATM spread is 25.6% of mid and ATM IV of 30.6 sits against 15.7 realised, so the implied number is noisy; the name's own median reaction is 1.76%. Run-up: +9.3% over 20 days, +2.7% over 5 days, -6.5% from the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 cooling demand in Entergy's census regions ran well above normal and above last year. AGA cooling degree days (weighted to AC customers) to 2026-09-26: West South Central cumulative 2,512 vs 2,241 last year (+12.1%) and normal 2,093 (+20%); about 528 CDD in September alone vs about 344 normal. East South Central cumulative +11.1% YoY. National August +22.3% YoY. Entergy booked +$0.06/share of weather vs normal in Q3 2025 and -$0.02 YTD through Q2 2026, so Q3 2026 weather plausibly adds several cents vs a normal-weather consensus of about $1.72.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 had a +$0.06 weather benefit and a narrowed guide; the stock moved +0.46%. Last seven reactions have a median |move| of 1.76%, with 5 of 7 up. Utility weather beats are usually treated as low quality.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side quarterly estimates are usually built on normal weather. If the market had priced the hot August and September, Q3 estimates would have risen over the quarter. Instead chartmill reports Entergy's next-quarter revenue estimate cut 4.2% over three months, and consensus EPS of about $1.72 is +12% on the year ago, in line with the guided growth rate and not above it.
findings.independence: Company YTD weather figures from the Q2 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65984/000006598426000279/earningsrelease2q26_ex991.htm) give the comparison base. CenterPoint (Houston, same WSC region) booked +$0.03 of favourable weather and usage in its Q3 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001130310/000110465926118963/tm2628051d1_ex99-1.htm). This is a proxy: a regional series, not Entergy's own number.

findings.finding: Three regulated peers that reported after Entergy last spoke beat and lifted outlooks. AEP (2026-10-28): operating EPS $2.23 vs about $2.04 consensus, 2026 guided at or above the top of $6.25-6.55, new 2027/2028 guides, $100B capex plan. CenterPoint (2026-10-27): $0.53 vs about $0.50, raised 2026 guide and a $70.7B plan, with Houston industrial throughput +11% YTD. FirstEnergy beat at $0.98 vs $0.90 and reaffirmed. This sets a sector bar of a beat plus an outlook lift on data-center load.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 raised the longer-term outlook: +1.33%. Q2 2026 affirmed only (with a $2.175B equity raise in the quarter): -4.03%. Q3 2025 narrowed and extended outlooks: +0.46%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. ETR is up 9.3% in 20 days, from about $104-106 around 10-21 to $110.28, which is consistent with the sector re-rating on these prints. What would still be unpriced is ETR-specific: a raised 2026 guide or capex lift. If the market expected that, ETR would be at its 52-week high ($118); it is 6.5% below it. The flip side: having watched AEP and CNP raise, the market may now penalise an affirm-only result, as in Q2 (-4.03%).
findings.independence: CenterPoint 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001130310/000110465926118963/tm2628051d1_ex99-1.htm) and the FirstEnergy summary (https://247wallst.com/cards/firstenergy-q3-2026-earnings-fe-01m5zha84d051svv1yr0f969wk) are separate companies' documents. All three are read-across and not Entergy's own number.

findings.finding: Guidance arithmetic: YTD adjusted EPS is $1.90 against a $4.25-4.45 guide. A Q3 at the $1.72 consensus leaves $0.73 for Q4 to reach the $4.40 FY consensus, already in the upper half of the range. A weather-aided Q3 makes narrowing to the upper half ($4.35-4.45) feasible, which would merely match consensus. Narrowing around the midpoint would read as a soft cut. Entergy narrowed at Q3 in 2025 (to $3.85-3.95).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 narrowed the guide and extended outlooks: +0.46%. Q2 2026 affirmed with no lift: -4.03%.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus of $4.40 sits above the guide midpoint of $4.35, so the street already leans to the upper half. The unpriced part is only the direction of the narrowing. If the market expected a top-of-range guide, FY consensus would sit near $4.45; it does not.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 narrowing precedent: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35753953/entergy-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results. Shares a document with finding 6 (the Q2 release) but rests on different numbers.

findings.finding: Regulatory friction in Arkansas. In early September 2026 the APSC denied Entergy Arkansas's request to buy power from the 440 MW Big Island solar plant, finding that costs and savings were not shown. It has opened docket 26-009-U on Entergy's treatment of production tax credits. The first base rate case in ten years (26-001-U, filed 2026-02-27) is pending. The 2026-10-19 Google phase-two package re-submits the Big Island PPA for approval.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned visibly on Arkansas regulation in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the denial is public since September and is small relative to the system. It could reach the stock on the call if management quantifies Arkansas rate-case risk, for example a settlement below the ask. If priced as a material risk, analysts would have cut 2027 estimates; the visible October cuts are price-target cuts (JPM, Barclays) without stated reasons.
findings.independence: Arkansas Advanced Energy tracker for 26-001-U and 26-009-U: https://www.arkansasadvancedenergy.com/entergy-arkansas-rate-case-2026. Mild positive skew points the same way.

findings.finding: October sell-side target moves are mixed to down: JPMorgan cut to $130 from $137 (Oct 13, overweight), Barclays cut to $115 from $128 (overweight), Truist set $119 (buy), Morgan Stanley raised to $101 from $98 (equal weight, Oct 21). The consensus target is about $120.78 (17 buy, 2 hold) against $110.28 spot.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock has rallied about 4% since these notes. They are filed because they show buy-side expectations are not euphoric going into the print.

findings.finding: Dilution runs into the quarter. Q2 diluted shares were 466.3M vs 445.7M a year earlier (+4.6%), and $3,056M of forward equity was still unsettled at 2026-06-30. Asked what the money buys: it funds a capex ramp corroborated by weather-adjusted industrial sales +12.3% YTD and retail +5.9% YTD, so it is not distress. Per-share drag is in consensus.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the share count and forwards are disclosed and modelled. Filed at zero because the financing question was answered as 'funds visible demand'.
findings.independence: Offering terms: https://rallies.ai/news/entergy-announces-2175-billion-stock-offering-with-32625-million-option-via-forward-sales; 8-K of 2026-09-02 on forward settlements: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000065984/000006598426000312/etr-20260902.htm

findings.finding: Entergy Arkansas announced phase two of its Google West Memphis partnership on 2026-10-19. Google funds about $600M of grid infrastructure (two batteries totalling 1,400 MWh, substation, two 230 kV lines) plus a 440 MW solar PPA, with $500M+ of claimed customer savings from 2028. The Q3 call gives management a fresh data-center talking point, but the EPS path is unclear because the funding comes from Google.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A data-center contract re-rating day in March 2026 saw shares +7.7% (https://rallies.ai/news/entergy-surges-as-data-center-contract-economics-and-regulatory-risk-outlook-re-rate); no print reaction tied to this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for 11 days and small. The only unpriced part is whether the call attaches rate base or load (GW) to it; the release gave neither.
findings.independence: https://mgrid.org/2026/10/20/google-takes-on-the-big-island-solar-ppa-arkansas-regulators-rejected-in-a-600-million-second-phase-with-entergy/ (same event, skeptical read). Shares the event with finding 4.

findings.finding: Volume momentum into Q3: weather-adjusted industrial sales were +9.9% in Q2 and +12.3% YTD, and retail +5.7% in Q2 and +5.9% YTD, against Q3 2025's +7.3% industrial and +4.4% retail.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: it is inside the growth the company guided to and is in consensus. A deceleration would be the surprise.
findings.independence: CenterPoint Houston industrial throughput +11% YTD (same Gulf Coast industrial base): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001130310/000110465926118963/tm2628051d1_ex99-1.htm. Shares a document with findings 3 and 6.

Entergy Arkansas base rate case 26-001-U (filed 2026-02-27) decision, likely around year-end under the Arkansas statutory clock.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean cuts mildly against the +2.75 downside skew and arrives after a +9.3% 20-day run-up that has likely already absorbed the peer beat-and-raise tone, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (documents beat inference; 'none was reasoning from weather') and lesson 1 (a weather beat is low-quality on a name whose Q3 2025 weather beat bought +0.46%): weather finding cut from +0.6 to +0.4 and p_up from 56 to 55, so expected_move falls from +0.34 to +0.28.
Lesson 6 (inside what the company guided): industrial/retail volume finding cut from +0.1 to +0.05.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): dilution finding left at 0.0 because the money funds a corroborated ramp.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (about 4% of float, 5.5 days, not crowded) and the skew is mild, so the Arkansas negative stays at -0.2.
Peer-print finding left at +0.3: a peer printing after the company last spoke is the pattern this file lists as having worked.
